<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Pervasiveness of Estimates</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities.  Disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of consolidated revenues and expenses during the reporting period is also required.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Cash, Temporary Cash Investments and Book Overdrafts</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Cash and temporary cash investments represent store cash and short-term investments with original maturities of less than three months. <td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Deposits In-Transit</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Deposits in-transit generally represent funds deposited to the Company&#8217;s bank accounts at the end of the year related to sales, a majority of which were paid for with debit cards, credit cards and checks, to which the Company does not have immediate access but settle within a few days of the sales transaction.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_InventoryPolicyTextBlock', window );">Inventories</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Inventories</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (principally on a last-in, first-out &#8220;LIFO&#8221; basis) or market.&#160; In total, approximately 89% of inventories in 2022 and 91% of inventories in 2021 were valued using the LIFO method.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> The remaining inventories, including substantially all fuel inventories, are stated at the lower of cost (on a FIFO basis) or net realizable value.  Replacement cost was higher than the carrying amount by </span>$2,196 at January 28, 2023 and $1,570 at January 29, 2022.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> The Company follows the Link-Chain, Dollar-Value LIFO method for purposes of calculating its LIFO charge or credit.  </span>During 2020, the Company had a LIFO liquidation primarily related to pharmacy inventory. The liquidated inventory was carried at lower costs prevailing in prior years as compared with current costs. The effect of this reduction in inventory decreased &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; by approximately $76, $58 net of tax. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The item-cost method of accounting to determine inventory cost before the LIFO adjustment is followed for substantially all store inventories at the Company&#8217;s supermarket divisions.&#160; This method involves counting each item in inventory, assigning costs to each of these items based on the actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts) of each item and recording the cost of items sold.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The item-cost method of accounting allows for more accurate reporting of periodic inventory balances and enables management to more precisely manage inventory.  In addition, substantially all of the Company&#8217;s inventory consists of finished goods and is recorded at actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts).</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company evaluates inventory shortages throughout the year based on actual physical counts in its facilities.  Allowances for inventory shortages are recorded based on the results of these counts to provide for estimated shortages as of the financial statement date.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock', window );">Property, Plant and Equipment</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Property, Plant and Equipment</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Property, plant and equipment are recorded at cost or, in the case of assets acquired in a business combination, at fair value.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> Depreciation and amortization expense, which includes the depreciation of assets recorded under finance leases, is computed principally using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of individual assets.  Buildings and land improvements are depreciated based on lives varying from </span>10 to 40 years.&#160; All new purchases of store equipment are assigned lives varying from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_bmfkYxgdMEmTcgB4lqE70Q;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">three</span></span> to nine years<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.  Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the lease term to which they relate, which generally varies from </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_CksJWFZwWEOUQv6Se4JtTg;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">four</span></span> to 25 years, or the useful life of the asset.&#160; Food production plant, fulfillment center and distribution center equipment is depreciated over lives varying from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_Jeq5E2ApREKpuhUbcA4W_Q;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">three</span></span> to 15 years<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">.  Information technology assets are generally depreciated over </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_SprxYSh6IEGvdt9XnKmCrw;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">three</span></span> to five years.&#160; Depreciation and amortization expense was $2,965 in 2022, $2,824 in 2021 and $2,747 in 2020.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Interest costs on significant projects constructed for the Company&#8217;s own use are capitalized as part of the costs of the newly constructed facilities.&#160; Upon retirement or disposal of assets, the cost and related accumulated depreciation and amortization are removed from the balance sheet and any gain or loss is reflected in net earnings.  Refer to Note 3 for further information regarding the Company&#8217;s property, plant and equipment.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock', window );">Leases</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Leases</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company leases certain store real estate, warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, office space and equipment.  The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception.  Finance and operating lease assets and liabilities are recognized at the lease commencement date.  Finance and operating lease liabilities represent the present value of minimum lease payments not yet paid. Operating lease assets represent the right to use an underlying asset and are based upon the operating lease liabilities adjusted for prepayments, lease incentives and impairment, if any. To determine the present value of lease payments, the Company estimates an incremental borrowing rate which represents the rate used for a secured borrowing of a similar term as the lease.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Lease terms generally range from 10 to 20 years with options to renew for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_eaBsLANZFkegxm8nzt8eIA;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">varying</span></span> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_tPEBD9uc902nL7BEnZF2bw;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">terms</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> at the Company&#8217;s sole discretion. The lease term includes the initial contractual term as well as any options to extend the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise that option. Leases with an initial term of 12 months or less are not recorded on the balance sheet.  Certain leases include escalation clauses or payment of executory costs such as property taxes, utilities or insurance and maintenance.  Operating lease payments are charged on a straight-line basis to rent expense over the lease term and finance lease payments are charged to interest expense and depreciation and amortization expense over the lease term.  Assets under finance leases are amortized in accordance with the Company&#8217;s normal depreciation policy for owned assets or over the lease term, if shorter.  The Company&#8217;s lease agreements do not contain any residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.  For additional information on leases, see Note 9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>
</td>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy', window );">Goodwill</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Goodwill</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company reviews goodwill for impairment during the fourth quarter of each year, or earlier upon the occurrence of a triggering event.  The Company performs reviews of each of its operating divisions and other consolidated entities (collectively, &#8220;reporting units&#8221;) that have goodwill balances.  Generally, fair value is determined using a market multiple model, or discounted projected future cash flows, and is compared to the carrying value of a reporting unit for purposes of identifying potential impairment.  Projected future cash flows are based on management&#8217;s knowledge of the current operating environment and expectations for the future.  Goodwill impairment is recognized for any excess of the reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value over its fair value, not to exceed the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit.  Results of the goodwill impairment reviews performed during 2022, 2021 and 2020 are summarized in Note 2.</span></p><span></span>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company monitors the carrying value of long-lived assets for potential impairment each quarter based on whether certain triggering events have occurred.&#160; These events include current period losses combined with a history of losses or a projection of continuing losses or a significant decrease in the market value of an asset.&#160; When a triggering event occurs, an impairment calculation is performed, comparing projected undiscounted future cash flows, utilizing current cash flow information and expected growth rates related to specific stores, to the carrying value for those stores.  If the Company identifies impairment for long-lived assets to be held and used, the Company compares the assets&#8217; current carrying value to the assets&#8217; fair value.  Fair value is based on current market values or discounted future cash flows.  The Company records impairment when the carrying value exceeds fair market value.  With respect to owned property and equipment held for disposal, the value of the property and equipment is adjusted to reflect recoverable values based on previous efforts to dispose of similar assets and current economic conditions.&#160; Impairment is recognized for the excess of the carrying value over the estimated fair market value, reduced by estimated direct costs of disposal.  The Company recorded asset impairments totaling $68, $64 and $70<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> in 2022, 2021 and 2020, respectively.  Costs to reduce the carrying value of long-lived assets for each of the years presented have been included in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as Operating, general and administrative (&#8220;OG&amp;A&#8221;) expense.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Store Closing Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company regularly evaluates the performance of its stores and periodically closes those stores that are underperforming.&#160; Related liabilities arise, such as severance, contractual obligations and other accruals associated with store closings.&#160; The Company records a liability for costs associated with an exit or disposal activity when the liability is incurred, usually in the period the store closes.&#160; Adjustments to closed store liabilities primarily relate to actual exit costs differing from original estimates. <td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Benefit Plans and Multi-Employer Pension Plans</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company recognizes the funded status of its retirement plans on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. <td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Share Based Compensation</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes compensation expense for all share-based payments granted under fair value recognition provisions. <td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock', window );">Deferred Income Taxes</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Deferred Income Taxes</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Deferred income taxes are recorded to reflect the tax consequences of differences between the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting basis.&#160; Refer to Note 4 for the types of differences that give rise to significant portions of deferred income tax assets and liabilities.&#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_IncomeTaxUncertaintiesPolicy', window );">Uncertain Tax Positions</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Uncertain Tax Positions</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company reviews the tax positions taken or expected to be taken on tax returns to determine whether and to what extent a benefit can be recognized in its consolidated financial statements.  Refer to Note 4 for the amount of unrecognized tax benefits and other related disclosures related to uncertain tax positions.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Various taxing authorities periodically audit the Company&#8217;s income tax returns.&#160; These audits include questions regarding the Company&#8217;s tax filing positions, including the timing and amount of deductions and the allocation of income to various tax jurisdictions.&#160; In evaluating the exposures connected with these various tax filing positions, including state and local taxes, the Company records allowances for probable exposures.&#160; A number of years may elapse before a particular matter, for which an allowance has been established, is audited and fully resolved.&#160; As of January 28, 2023, the years ended February 1, 2020 and forward remain open for review for federal income tax purposes.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The assessment of the Company&#8217;s tax position relies on the judgment of management to estimate the exposures associated with the Company&#8217;s various filing positions.</p><span></span>

<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock', window );">Revenue Recognition</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">Sales</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14.35pt;"><span style="margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">The Company recognizes revenues from the</span> retail <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> products, net of sales taxes,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">at</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the point</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">of</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;">sale.  Pharmacy sales</span> are<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> recorded when the </span>product is<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>provided <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;"> customer.  Digital channel originated sales are recognized either upon pickup in store or upon delivery to the customer.  </span>Amounts billed to a customer related to shipping and delivery represent revenues earned for the goods provided and are classified as sales.&#160;<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> When shipping is discounted, it is recorded as an adjustment to sales.  </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Discounts provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to customers</span> by<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> the Company</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">at</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the time</span> of <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">including</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">those</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in connection with</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">loyalty</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cards,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">are recognized as </span>a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">reduction</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in sales</span> as <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the products </span>are<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> sold.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Discounts provided </span>by<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> vendors, usually in</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">form</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> coupons, are</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">not recognized </span>as a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">reduction</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">in</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sales provided</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> coupons</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>are <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">redeemable</span> at <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">any retailer that</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">accepts</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">coupons.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">The</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">records </span>a <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">receivable </span>from<span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>the vendor<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>for the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> difference</span> in <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sales price</span> and <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cash received.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.5pt;"> </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">For merchandise sold in one of the Company&#8217;s stores or online, tender is accepted at the point of sale.  The Company acts as principal in certain vendor arrangements where the purchase and sale of inventory are virtually simultaneous. The Company records revenue and related costs on a gross basis for these arrangements.&#160; For pharmacy sales, collection of third-party receivables is typically expected within </span>three months<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> or less from the time of purchase.  The third-party receivables from pharmacy sales are recorded in &#8220;Receivables&#8221; in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets and were </span>$867 as of January 28, 2023 and $774 as of January 29, 2022.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">Gift Cards and Gift Certificates</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:2.3pt;margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 5.3pt 0pt 0pt;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">The</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">does</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>not<span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognize</span> revenue<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> when</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">it</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sells</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">its</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">own gift</span> cards<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>gift <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">certificates (collectively &#8220;gift cards&#8221;).</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.4pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Rather, it records </span>a<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> deferred revenue </span>liability equal to <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">amount</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> received.</span><span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"> </span>A <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">sale</span> is <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">then</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognized when</span> the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> gift</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">cards</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">are</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">redeemed</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">to purchase</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company&#8217;s</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;">products.  The Company&#8217;s gift cards do not expire.  While gift cards are generally redeemed within </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">12 months</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">, some are never fully redeemed. The</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">Company</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognizes gift card</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">breakage under the</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">proportional</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">method,</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">where</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">recognition</span> <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">of breakage income</span> is based<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>upon <span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">the historical</span> run-off<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>rate<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> unredeemed gift cards.</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">  The Company&#8217;s gift card deferred revenue liability was </span>$200 as of January 28, 2023 and $185 as of January 29, 2022.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt 5.3pt 0pt 0pt;"><i <tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_kr_MerchandiseCostsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Merchandise Costs</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Merchandise Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations includes product costs, net of discounts and allowances; advertising costs (see separate discussion below); inbound freight charges; warehousing costs, including receiving and inspection costs; transportation costs; and food production and operational costs.&#160; Warehousing, transportation and manufacturing management salaries are also included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item; however, purchasing management salaries and administration costs are included in the &#8220;OG&amp;A&#8221; line item along with most of the Company&#8217;s other managerial and administrative costs.&#160; Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company&#8217;s digital offerings originating from non-retail store locations are included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item.  Rent expense and depreciation and amortization expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Warehousing and transportation costs include distribution center direct wages, transportation direct wages, repairs and maintenance, utilities, inbound freight and, where applicable, third-party warehouse management fees.&#160; These costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company believes the classification of costs included in merchandise costs could vary widely throughout the industry.&#160; The Company&#8217;s approach is to include in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item the direct, net costs of acquiring products and making them available to customers.&#160; The Company believes this approach most accurately presents the actual costs of products sold.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes all vendor allowances as a reduction in merchandise costs when the related product is sold.&#160; When possible, vendor allowances are applied to the related product cost by item and, therefore, reduce the carrying value of inventory by item.&#160; When the items are sold, the vendor allowance is recognized.&#160; When it is not possible, due to systems constraints, to allocate vendor allowances to the product by item, vendor allowances are recognized as a reduction in merchandise costs based on inventory turns and, therefore, recognized as the product is sold.</p><span></span>
</td>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Advertising Costs</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s advertising costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred and are included in the &#8220;Merchandise costs&#8221; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160; The Company&#8217;s advertising costs totaled $1,030 in 2022, $984 in 2021 and $888 in 2020.&#160; The Company does not record vendor allowances for co-operative advertising as a reduction of advertising expense.</p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Operating, General and Administrative Expenses</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">OG&amp;A expenses consist primarily of employee-related costs such as wages, healthcare benefit costs, retirement plan costs, utilities, and credit card fees. Rent expense, depreciation and amortization expense and interest expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">For purposes of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, the Company considers all highly liquid debt instruments purchased with an original maturity of three months or less to be temporary cash investments.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><span></span>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock', window );">Segments</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Segments</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Company operates supermarkets, multi-department stores and fulfillment centers throughout the United States.  The Company&#8217;s retail operations, which represent </span>97%<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> of the Company&#8217;s consolidated sales, are its only reportable segment.  The Company aggregates its operating divisions into </span>one<span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"> reportable segment due to the operating divisions having similar economic characteristics with similar long-term financial performance.  In addition, the Company&#8217;s operating divisions offer customers similar products, have similar distribution methods, operate in similar regulatory environments, purchase the majority of the merchandise for retail sale from similar (and in many cases identical) vendors on a coordinated basis from a centralized location, serve similar types of customers, and are allocated capital from a centralized location.  Operating divisions are organized primarily on a geographical basis so that the operating division management team can be responsive to local needs of the operating division and can execute company strategic plans and initiatives throughout the locations in their operating division. This geographical separation is the primary differentiation between these retail operating divisions.  The geographical basis of organization reflects how the business is managed and how the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, who acts as the Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker, assesses performance internally.  All of the Company&#8217;s operations are domestic.</span></p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Tabular disclosure of long-debt instruments or arrangements, including identification, terms, features, collateral requirements and other information necessary to a fair presentation. <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_CurrentFederalTaxExpenseBenefit">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount, after unamortized (discount) premium and debt issuance costs, of long-term debt, classified as current. <tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_DefinedBenefitPlanHealthCareCostTrendRateAssumedNextFiscalYear">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Assumed rate, for next fiscal year, based on annual change in cost of health care cost benefits used to measure expected cost of benefits covered by defined benefit postretirement plan. Factors include, but are not limited to, estimate of health care inflation, change in health care utilization or delivery pattern, technological advances, and change in health status of participant. <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_EscrowDeposit">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The designation of funds furnished by a borrower to a lender to assure future payments of the borrower's real estate taxes and insurance obligations with respect to a mortgaged property. Escrow deposits may be made for a variety of other purposes such as earnest money and contingent payments. This element excludes replacement reserves which are an escrow separately provided for within the US GAAP taxonomy.</p></div>
